title: How far? The extent of chemical change
summary: Reversible reactions reach dynamic equilibrium. Write equilibrium constant expressions, interpret K and use Le Châtelier's principle; at HL, the reaction quotient, equilibrium calculations and the link to Gibbs energy.

keyterms.definition: State of a reversible reaction in a closed system where forward and backward rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.
A system in which matter cannot enter or leave, though energy can be exchanged.
Ratio of product to reactant concentrations at equilibrium, each raised to its coefficient; constant at a given temperature.
If a system at equilibrium is disturbed, the position of equilibrium shifts to partially counteract the change.
The relative amounts of reactants and products at equilibrium; "shifts right" means more products.
Industrial synthesis of ammonia: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH < 0, using an iron catalyst at a compromise temperature and high pressure.
A reaction that can proceed in both forward and backward directions, shown by ⇌.
Same expression as K but using concentrations at any moment; compare with K to predict direction.
Initial–Change–Equilibrium table used to calculate equilibrium concentrations or K.
When K is very small, the change x is negligible compared with initial concentrations, simplifying calculations.

options: forward and backward rates are equal
reactant and product concentrations are equal
questions.explanation: Both reactions continue at equal rates, so concentrations are constant (but not necessarily equal).
Each concentration is raised to the power of its coefficient.

questions.statement: A very large value of K means the equilibrium mixture contains mostly products.
questions.explanation: K ≫ 1: products dominate; K ≪ 1: reactants dominate.

questions.prompt: If the equation 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (K) is reversed, the new constant is…
questions.explanation: Reversing swaps numerator and denominator.

questions.prompt: Match each change to the effect on K (exothermic forward reaction).
questions.explanation: Only temperature changes the value of K; catalysts, pressure and concentration do not.

questions.statement: Equilibrium can be established in an open beaker from which a gaseous product escapes.
questions.explanation: A closed system is needed; escaping product prevents the backward reaction.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct K expression for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)?
questions.explanation: Products over reactants, each raised to its coefficient.

questions.text: A reaction that can go in both directions is shown with the symbol ___.
questions.explanation: The double half-arrow indicates reversibility.

questions.prompt: Order the events as H₂ and I₂ are sealed in a flask and heated.
items: Forward rate is at its maximum
HI forms and the backward rate begins
Forward rate falls as reactants are used
Forward and backward rates become equal
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is reached when rates are equal.

questions.prompt: If K = 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ at 298 K, the reaction…
questions.explanation: A tiny K means very little product at equilibrium. K tells nothing about rate.

questions.prompt: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH < 0, increasing the pressure…
questions.explanation: The right has fewer gas moles (2 vs 4), so the system shifts right to reduce pressure.

questions.statement: Increasing the temperature of an exothermic equilibrium shifts it to the left.
questions.explanation: The system absorbs the added heat by favouring the endothermic (backward) reaction; K decreases.

questions.prompt: Adding a catalyst to an equilibrium mixture…
options: allows equilibrium to be reached faster without changing position
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds forward and backward reactions equally.

questions.text: Removing a product from an equilibrium mixture shifts the position to the ___.
questions.explanation: The system makes more product to replace what was removed.

questions.prompt: Match each Haber process choice to its reason.
questions.explanation: Industrial conditions balance yield, rate, cost and safety.

questions.statement: For H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), increasing pressure changes the equilibrium position.
questions.explanation: There are equal gas moles on both sides (2 and 2), so pressure has no effect on position.

questions.prompt: [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ (pink) + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CoCl₄]²⁻ (blue) + 6H₂O is endothermic. On cooling the solution turns…
questions.explanation: Cooling favours the exothermic (backward) reaction, forming pink [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺.

questions.text: The only factor that changes the value of K is ___.
questions.explanation: Other changes shift position but leave K unchanged.

questions.prompt: Order the reasoning when extra N₂ is added to the Haber equilibrium.
items: Forward rate temporarily exceeds backward rate
New equilibrium with more NH₃, same K
questions.explanation: The disturbance is partially counteracted, not removed.

questions.prompt: Why is the Haber process not run at a very low temperature even though yield is higher?
options: The rate would be too slow
The catalyst works better when cold
questions.explanation: Low temperature gives a high equilibrium yield but too slow a rate to be economic.

options: proceeds forward to make more products
questions.explanation: Q must rise to K, so products are formed.

questions.statement: Q has the same mathematical form as K.
questions.explanation: Q uses current (non-equilibrium) concentrations in the same expression.

questions.text: For A ⇌ 2B with [A] = 0.40 and [B] = 0.20 mol dm⁻³ at equilibrium, K = ___.

questions.prompt: 1.00 mol each of H₂ and I₂ in 1.00 dm³ form 1.60 mol HI at equilibrium. K =

questions.explanation: ΔG⦵ = −RT ln K.

questions.statement: The small-K approximation assumes that x is negligible compared with the initial concentration.
questions.explanation: It works when K is very small, e.g. for weak acids.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of an ICE-table calculation.
items: Express changes in terms of x using the mole ratio
Substitute into the K expression and solve
questions.explanation: Changes must follow the stoichiometry.

questions.prompt: K = 4.0 for A + B ⇌ C. At one moment [A] = [B] = 0.50 and [C] = 2.0 mol dm⁻³. The reaction…
questions.explanation: Q = 2.0/(0.50 × 0.50) = 8.0 > K, so the reaction proceeds backward.
Links thermodynamics to the equilibrium constant.

questions.prompt: Which statement about K is correct?
options: K changes when a catalyst is added
questions.explanation: K at a given temperature is fixed regardless of starting amounts.
